decision.title: Approve AI-Assisted Loan Underwriting Model v3.2
decision.description: Decision to deploy updated machine learning model for consumer loan underwriting. Model trained on 2.1M historical applications with fairness constraints applied.
decision.outcome: Approved with conditions: quarterly bias audit, 6-month sunset review, manual override required for applications >$500K
decision.rationale: Model demonstrates 12% improvement in default prediction accuracy while maintaining disparate impact ratio within regulatory thresholds. Council identified anchoring bias in initial risk assessment — mitigated via blind re-evaluation. Dissenting CISO opinion on data residency preserved.

agents.perspective: Financial risk and return analysis. Model improves loss ratios by estimated $4.2M annually. Recommends deployment with enhanced monitoring.
Security and data governance concerns. Training data includes EU citizen records — GDPR Article 22 automated decision-making safeguards required. Data residency conflict between US and EU processing.
Regulatory compliance assessment. ECOA and fair lending obligations met based on disparate impact testing. Recommends documenting model limitations for examiner readiness.
Operational risk evaluation. Model concentration risk in certain demographic segments. Stress testing under adverse economic scenarios shows acceptable degradation.

messages.content: The model's improved accuracy translates to $4.2M in reduced losses annually. NPV positive within 8 months. I recommend immediate deployment to the consumer lending division.
messages.reasoning: Based on backtesting against 18 months of held-out data

messages.content: I have concerns about data residency. The training dataset includes 340K EU citizen records processed on US infrastructure. Under GDPR Article 44, this requires either adequacy decisions or appropriate safeguards. I recommend a data localization review before deployment.
messages.reasoning: Cross-border data transfer compliance gap identified

messages.content: Fair lending analysis is favorable. Disparate impact ratios: gender 0.94, race 0.91, age 0.89 — all within the four-fifths rule threshold. However, I note the age ratio is approaching the boundary and recommend quarterly monitoring.
messages.reasoning: ECOA compliance verified via standard DI testing methodology

messages.content: Stress testing reveals the model degrades significantly in high-unemployment scenarios (>8%). Default prediction accuracy drops from 94% to 76%. I recommend a circuit breaker that reverts to the previous model if unemployment exceeds 7%.
messages.reasoning: Monte Carlo simulation with 10,000 economic scenarios

votes.rationale: Financial benefits outweigh identified risks with proposed safeguards
Approve only after data residency review and EU processing safeguards implemented
votes.conditions: Complete GDPR Article 44 assessment and implement data localization for EU records

votes.rationale: Fair lending compliance verified. Quarterly monitoring addresses age ratio concern
Approve with unemployment circuit breaker at 7%
votes.conditions: Implement automatic model reversion trigger when unemployment rate exceeds 7%

dissent.content: The data residency issue is not a minor compliance gap — it represents a fundamental architectural decision that should have been addressed during model training. Deploying before resolving cross-border transfer mechanisms creates regulatory exposure that could result in GDPR enforcement action. I formally dissent from any deployment timeline that does not include a completed Data Protection Impact Assessment.

alternativesConsidered.description: Delay deployment 6 months to retrain model on region-specific data
alternativesConsidered.rejectionRationale: Would forfeit $2.1M in estimated loss reduction. Quarterly monitoring addresses fairness concerns without full retrain.
alternativesConsidered.riskAssessment: Low risk — monitoring catches degradation before material impact

alternativesConsidered.description: Deploy only for US applicants initially (phased rollout)
alternativesConsidered.rejectionRationale: Accepted as a condition — EU deployment deferred pending GDPR assessment
alternativesConsidered.riskAssessment: Adopted as mitigation for CISO's data residency concern

biasesDetected.evidence: CFO's initial $4.2M figure dominated subsequent discussion. No independent financial analysis was performed by other agents.

conflicts: GDPR Article 44: Cross-border transfer safeguards required for EU citizen training data
